hero.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
hero.teaser: Riviera Beach was selected as one of just 10 communities nationwide to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city recognized this year.
hero.body:
Riviera Beach has been selected as one of only 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the sole Florida city honored this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that successfully unite residents, local government, businesses and organizations to address local challenges and create meaningful change. City leaders presented Riviera Beach's accomplishments during the National Civic League conference in Denver, where judges announced the city as a first-time winner.

Mayor Douglas Lawson expressed pride in the recognition, stating "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars." Lawson credited the award to the city's long-term commitment to revitalization and improving quality of life. He noted that residents are witnessing the changes and reimagining of Riviera Beach that leaders have worked toward for years. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson highlighted the community's role in the achievement, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents. Every event we host, every project we complete, and every challenge we overcome happens because our community shows up for one another."

The city's application emphasized three key civic engagement programs. The Riviera Beach Youth Council engages high school students in civic leadership and advocacy work. The Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education program, achieved a 98% completion rate. The Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program provides mini-grants to longtime homeowners for critical home repairs. These initiatives reflect the city's broader approach to treating civic engagement as a partnership between government, residents, faith groups, schools and community organizations. Miller-Anderson explained that the city is "doing a lot of innovative things to make sure that our community is able to say that they are part of what's happening here in the city."

The All-America City Award, presented annually since 1949, is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors. City officials say the designation celebrates Riviera Beach's progress while positioning the community for future opportunities and growth. The award sends a message to the nation that Riviera Beach is a place where collaboration produces results and residents play an active role in shaping their community's future. The nine other cities receiving the 2026 award are Chelsea, Massachusetts; Franklin, Tennessee; Harlingen, Texas; Montgomery, Alabama; Morrisville, North Carolina; Norfolk, Virginia; North Charleston, South Carolina; Roanoke, Virginia; and Woodburn, Oregon.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, though he said he was not trying to set a record after vetoing $3.1 billion in 2022. DeSantis described the vetoed items as either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. It sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. However, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement, but that transfer was among the cuts.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 budget projects worth $830 million that the group labeled as turkeys. The Governor vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting the Legislature to include the potential $750 million transfer this year.

DeSantis indicated he would not formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked. The budget represents the final major spending plan of DeSantis' tenure as Governor, capping years of aggressive use of veto power to shape state priorities.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's order to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate a teacher suspended last year following controversial social media .
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board is pushing back against a judge's recommendation to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009 who was suspended last year following controversial social media comments about Charlie Kirk. In a Thursday court filing, the school board argued that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending Theobald get his job back, saying "numerous findings ... are not based upon competent substantial evidence." The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post about Kirk, which labeled him as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi, was a "serious offense" and removing him was appropriate.

In an order issued last month, Livingstone cited a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that said disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board still has the final say on whether Theobald gets his job back. After the judge's recommendation, Theobald told WPTV the case raises questions about where the line is drawn for teachers speaking outside of school. It's unclear when a final decision will be made.

cards.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters hit waterways
cards.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deployed two boats with medics for the holiday weekend as hundreds of boaters celebrate on local waterways.
cards.body:
Hundreds of boaters are heading to Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting the Martin County Maritime Response Unit to increase patrols. Lt. Brett Harry said his team is expecting a significant surge in boating activity and will have two boats staffed with medics positioned in the north and south areas of Martin County on standby. The maritime unit is prepared to respond to a wide range of emergencies, from minor incidents like stubbed toes to serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety during their holiday outings. Harry urged all boaters to take precautions by keeping their eyes on the water, designating a driver who won't consume alcohol, and carrying life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said, encouraging holiday celebrants to enjoy the weekend while remaining vigilant.

cards.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute at JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands to resolve
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons.
cards.body:
A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating conflict between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with potential expenses in the thousands to fix the problem. Residents at the Colony Condos contend that people accessing the JB-7 public walkway have been cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. With only bushes now marking the boundary between the public path and private land, trespassing has become increasingly common during peak summer months.

Lori Hill, who lives at the Colony Condos, described how the issue intensifies when warm weather arrives. She explained that beachgoers park in private spots and push back bushes to access the sand with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill noted that residents once confronted trespassers directly but have shifted to calling police to handle the problem. She said the fence previously made the property line obvious to visitors. However, not all beachgoers acknowledge the issue. Michael House, who walks to JB-7 from a public parking lot blocks away, said he has not observed the trespassing problems residents describe. "There's plenty of free parking," House said. "If they're damaging property and you know littering and stuff like that might be a different issue."

The matter reached the Juno Beach Town Council during a recent meeting. A town official stated that the municipality is not legally required to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern suggested exploring less expensive options than a full fence replacement. "I understand fencing is expensive, but I'd like to see maybe we can help them with a lower-cost fence or some combination of split rail and shrubs," Halpern said. The council decided to address the fence question during its budget discussions scheduled for July 15.

Hill expressed optimism that the town will take action on the issue. "We're really hoping that the town will get back on board and just put it back up, so that we can have our landscaping and our private parking," she said. The outcome will likely depend on how town officials prioritize the expense during their upcoming budget deliberations and whether they determine a lower-cost alternative could adequately address the problem.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after Anthem denies coverage hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to have a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for the procedure. According to her denial letter, the surgery involved a surgical mesh called GalaFlex, which the insurer considered "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body but not for breast reconstruction, making it an off-label treatment. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that the mesh's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and has become a vocal critic of insurance denials, joining doctors taking their frustrations to social media and calling out insurers by name. She contends the product is less risky than other options with proven success. Despite Anthem's denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with the GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago. Anthem stated it regularly reviews coverage policies to ensure they are based on medical evidence and aligned with the latest treatment standards, but without FDA approval for breast reconstruction, the mesh does not meet their coverage standards. Last year, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to start approving GalaFlex for breast reconstruction.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive 'A' rating from state
cards.teaser: For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an 'A' rating from the state, continuing a streak district leaders say reflects strong student performance across all grade levels.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received an "A" or "B" rating, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district achieved a record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. Additionally, 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework through Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment courses, and 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

One of the district's biggest success stories came from S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach, which jumped from a "C" rating to an "A" this year under Principal Rona Tata's leadership. Three years ago, Tata's staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which serves students starting at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Spady Elementary was one of four district schools to improve from a "C" to an "A" rating this year. The others were Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Boca Raton High School band to represent Florida at National Independence Day Parade
cards.teaser: The Boca Raton Community High School band has earned a coveted spot in Washington, D.C.'s National Independence Day Parade and they'll be representing the entire state of Florida.
cards.body:
On July 4 at 10:30 a.m., the Boca Raton Community High School band will march a full mile along the National Mall in Washington, D.C., from Constitution Avenue to Independence Avenue, representing Florida at the National Independence Day Parade. Only bands nominated by state officials receive invitations to this prestigious event. Junior Lola Cabezas said there are millions, if not billions, of people watching. "It's a lot of pressure, but I think we'll be able to rise to the occasion," Cabezas said. She explained the physical demands of marching band, noting that performers must play, breathe, and walk while maintaining consistent sound without hearing their steps in the music.

Senior Stephin Restivo said the team is laser-focused on nailing every detail, including the marching and timing of everything. Band Director Jenn Girdlestone said she has full confidence in the students that they'll put their best foot forward, literally, and will rise to the occasion and represent the country well. For senior Lily Schaffer, making it to D.C. proves how far the program has come. "Getting to do this is an amazing opportunity," Schaffer said. "It shows how much we've grown and showcases what we do here, because this program is so amazing." The parade will be streamed live on YouTube for those who want to cheer on the band from home.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs rise 4% this year across Florida
cards.teaser: According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago.
cards.body:
According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The survey points to inflation as the primary driver of increased prices. Ground beef is up 5.5%, and buns are up 7.7%. Strawberries, hit hard by a Florida frost, are up 12.4%. Ice cream is up 5.3%. Not everything is more expensive, though. Potato prices are down this year, which is good news for potato chip and salad lovers. Corn prices have fluctuated, but locally grown corn from the Glades can offer the best deal.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch said there are ways to keep costs in check. She recommended shopping savvier than ever by comparing stores to see who has the best deals for groceries on your list. The biggest thing for families is cutting down food waste, which begins with a meal plan, Woroch said. Shoppers planning their Fourth of July menus reported plans ranging from hamburgers with coleslaw and chips to burnt ends with mashed potatoes and fresh broccoli.

hero.headline: Juno Beach residents demand new fence at JB-7 beach access as costs could reach thousands
hero.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say beachgoers using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023. The town council will address the issue in budget discussions on July 15.
hero.body:
Residents at the Colony Condos in Juno Beach are pushing the town to reinstall a fence at the JB-7 public beach access point after removing the barrier in 2023 for safety reasons created a trespassing problem. The missing fence has left only bushes to mark the boundary between the public walkway and the condominium's private property, allowing beachgoers to cut through private land while accessing the beach. During summer months, the issue intensifies as visitors park in reserved spots and push through vegetation to reach the sand with coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, described the situation as increasingly difficult for property owners who now rely on police to handle confrontational encounters with trespassers rather than attempting to address the problem themselves.

The problem gained attention at a recent Juno Beach Town Council meeting, where officials acknowledged the dispute but noted the town has no legal obligation to construct a fence. Hill explained that residents appreciated how the original fence made property boundaries obvious and prevented the current wave of unwanted visitors. Not all beachgoers agree that a serious problem exists. Michael House, a regular visitor to JB-7, said he walks to the access point from a nearby public parking lot and has not observed the trespassing issues that residents describe. He suggested that if property damage or littering occurs, those would be separate concerns worth addressing.

Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern indicated the town might explore more affordable alternatives to a full fence replacement. Halpern suggested considering a combination approach using split rail fencing paired with shrubs as a lower-cost solution that could still establish a clear boundary between public and private areas. This middle-ground proposal reflects recognition that fencing expenses could be substantial for the town's budget while still attempting to address resident concerns about unauthorized access.

The town council voted to include the fence question in its upcoming budget discussions scheduled for July 15. Hill and other Colony residents remain hopeful that the town will take action to restore both their landscaping and exclusive use of their private parking areas. The outcome will depend on whether town officials determine the cost is justified and whether a compromise solution like the split rail and shrub combination can effectively discourage trespassing while reducing expenses.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in home fire as community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out in her Hobe Sound home. Friends launched a fundraiser to help her fiance Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed their belongings.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her and her fiance's home in Hobe Sound. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have since launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of his and White's belongings.

Nina Fenn, a friend of White's for eight years, learned of the death through a phone call from White's fiance Mark. Fenn said the loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured after losing his only child, Jacob. White's birthday is the Fourth of July, adding another layer of heartbreak to the tragedy. Fenn described White as a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano. She was always the first to lend a hand and loved kids and people.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie moves forward with Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to transfer 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. According to Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, the interchange addresses a significant gap between existing Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples said the interchange will help accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth expected over the next 20 to 50 years.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to reduce congestion and improve safety. Crews are currently working on the first phase, widening the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road. The second phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design stage, with construction anticipated to begin in summer 2027. The widening project will also add bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks. The partial interchange for the Turnpike remains in the design phase. City Council will vote on final approval to transfer the land to FDOT at an upcoming meeting.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year, ground beef and strawberries see biggest increases
cards.teaser: A holiday cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
cards.body:
This year's Fourth of July cookout will cost families more than ever before. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The price increases are driven largely by inflation across multiple food categories. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, while buns increased 7.7%. Strawberries, hit particularly hard by a Florida frost, jumped 12.4%, and ice cream prices climbed 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have increased, however. Potato prices are down this year, offering relief to shoppers planning potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best value. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends families compare prices across stores to find the best deals and plan meals carefully to reduce food waste. Treasure Coast shoppers surveyed Friday described holiday plans featuring hamburgers, coleslaw, chips, burnt ends, mashed potatoes and fresh broccoli, highlighting the traditional cookout items now facing higher costs.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound woman dies in house fire, community raises funds for fiance
cards.teaser: Misty Dawn White, 46, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, of Hobe Sound, was found dead Monday after a fire broke out inside her home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause. The fire remains under investigation. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help White's fiancé Mark rebuild after the flames destroyed many of their belongings.

Nina Fenn, who has been friends with White for eight years, described the scene as "completely a state of devastation." Fenn said White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants and playing the piano, and was always the first to lend a hand. She noted that White's loss is compounded by grief Mark has already endured, as he lost his only child, Jacob, tragically. White's birthday was July 4, just days after her death on Monday. Fenn said White's memory will live on in the hearts of those who loved her, calling her "a good soul" who will always be remembered.

cards.headline: Insurance company denies Treasure Coast breast cancer patient reconstruction surgery hours before procedure
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago. Her insurance company, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield, denied coverage for her reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, a 48-year-old Treasure Coast resident diagnosed three months ago with invasive ductal carcinoma, underwent a full double bilateral mastectomy followed by reconstruction surgery using GalaFlex, a synthetic surgical mesh. However, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the reconstruction procedure less than 24 hours before it was scheduled. According to the denial letter, the surgery was deemed "investigational" with "no or not enough proof it improves health." While the FDA has approved GalaFlex for some uses in the body, it has not approved it for breast reconstruction. In a 2023 letter to health care providers, the FDA stated that "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Dr. Alicia Billington, Clark's plastic surgeon, uses GalaFlex mesh on most of her breast reconstruction patients and says it produces "the least amount of complications" compared to other options. Billington has joined doctors publicly criticizing insurance denials on social media. After investigative reporting last year shared breast cancer patients' denial stories, Cigna became the first and only major insurer to approve GalaFlex for breast reconstruction. Anthem stated the mesh "does not currently meet the standards required for coverage by our medical policy" without FDA approval. Despite the denial, Clark received her surgery more than a week ago. Clark and Billington continue fighting the denial as a new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act.

hero.headline: Martin County maritime teams on standby as Fourth of July boaters hit waterways
hero.teaser: Martin County Maritime Response Unit deployed two boats with medics for the holiday weekend as hundreds of boaters celebrate on local waterways.
hero.body:
Hundreds of boaters are heading to Florida waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting the Martin County Maritime Response Unit to increase patrols. Lt. Brett Harry said his team is expecting a significant surge in boating activity and will have two boats staffed with medics positioned in the north and south areas of Martin County on standby. The maritime unit is prepared to respond to a wide range of emergencies, from minor incidents like stubbed toes to serious medical events including cardiac emergencies and spinal injuries.

Boaters like Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who launched from Sandsprit Park in Martin County on Friday with their young daughter and puppy, are prioritizing safety during their holiday outings. Harry urged all boaters to take precautions by keeping their eyes on the water, designating a driver who won't consume alcohol, and carrying life vests, whistles and flotation devices. "Just have fun and be safe," Harry said, encouraging holiday celebrants to enjoy the weekend while remaining vigilant.

cards.headline: Hobe Sound community rallies around man who lost fiance in deadly home fire
cards.teaser: Friends launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after his fiance Misty Dawn White died in a Monday fire at their Hobe Sound home.
cards.body:
Misty Dawn White, 46, died Monday after a fire broke out inside her Hobe Sound home. Preliminary findings from the sheriff's office point to an electrical issue as a possible cause, though the fire remains under investigation. White's fiancé Mark called her friend Nina Fenn to inform her of the death.

Fenn, who was friends with White for eight years, said the flames destroyed many of Mark's and White's belongings. Friends have launched a fundraiser to help Mark rebuild after the fire left his home in a state of devastation. White was a Christian woman who loved gardening, plants, playing piano and helping people. The loss is especially difficult for Mark, who previously lost his only child Jacob. White's birthday was July 4, just days after her death on Monday. Fenn said White will always be remembered as a good soul who will remain in the hearts of those who loved her.

cards.headline: Martin County School Board fights judge's recommendation to reinstate teacher suspended over Charlie Kirk comments
cards.teaser: The school board filed a court motion Thursday challenging a judge's order to reinstate Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy suspended for Facebook comments about Charlie Kirk.
cards.body:
The Martin County School Board filed a court motion Thursday arguing that Administrative Law Judge Jodi-Ann Vanessa Livingstone erred in recommending the reinstatement of Matt Theobald, a social studies teacher at Spectrum Academy since 2009. Theobald was suspended last year after making social media comments labeling Charlie Kirk as racist, misogynistic and a neo-Nazi. The board's attorney claims Theobald's Facebook post was a "serious offense" and his removal was appropriate. In the Thursday filing, the board argued that "numerous findings" in the judge's recommendation "are not based upon competent substantial evidence."

Livingstone issued an order last month citing a recent Florida Fifth District Court of Appeal ruling that disciplining a teacher for personal Facebook posts made off school grounds, on personal equipment, with no student involvement, violated the teacher's First Amendment rights. The judge recommended Theobald be awarded back pay and benefits. According to an investigation report, Theobald admitted writing the comments about Kirk but said they were posted on his mother's private Facebook page "within a discussion among personal acquaintances" and were not intended for public view. The school board retains final authority on whether Theobald gets his job back.

cards.headline: Record Fourth of July travel brings heavy traffic and rain to Florida Turnpike
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, with 61.4 million traveling by car.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling for the Fourth of July weekend, creating heavy traffic and challenging conditions on South Florida roads. Friday's rain made driving particularly difficult on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd said the weather was beautiful until the rain started, noting that "everyone forgets how to drive" in wet conditions. Despite the weather, driver Jim Macfawn said he pressed on, explaining that his driving experience allowed him to "just roll with the punches." He was struck by the scale of travel this year, saying "It sounds like a lot. I'm surprised people can afford all the gas."

AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day. Experiences on the road varied widely. Carlos Borras reported smooth sailing on his round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday, seeing no traffic or accidents. However, driver Fernando Amado described heavy traffic, especially with the weather, noting that Saturday was the day when most people were heading north. AAA recommends traveling after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid congestion, with the heaviest traffic expected between 10 a.m. Saturday and noon to 6 p.m. Sunday.

cards.headline: Breast cancer patient speaks out after insurance denial hours before reconstruction surgery
cards.teaser: Beth Clark, 48, had her insurance coverage for breast reconstruction denied less than 24 hours before surgery by Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield.
cards.body:
Beth Clark, 48, was diagnosed with invasive ductal carcinoma three months ago and chose to undergo a full double bilateral mastectomy with reconstruction to eliminate any possibility of cancer recurrence. Less than 24 hours before her reconstruction surgery, Anthem Blue Cross and Blue Shield denied coverage for the procedure. According to the denial letter, the surgery involving GalaFlex surgical mesh is considered "investigational" with insufficient proof that it improves health. While GalaFlex is FDA-approved for some uses in the body, it is not approved for breast reconstruction and remains an off-label treatment. The FDA reiterated in a 2023 letter that the mesh's "efficacy and safety for breast cancer patients have not been determined."

Despite the denial, Clark received her reconstruction surgery with GalaFlex mesh a little more than a week ago after her surgeon, Dr. Alicia Billington, found a way to make it happen. Billington uses GalaFlex on most of her breast reconstruction patients and states the product produces the least amount of complications compared to other options. An Anthem spokesperson said the company regularly reviews coverage policies based on medical evidence and that the mesh does not currently meet their standards for coverage without FDA approval. Clark and Billington are continuing to fight the denial. A new bill has been introduced to modernize the Women's Health and Cancer Rights Act to protect breast cancer patients from treatment denials.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for a state title run during the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a distric.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots football team is preparing for a state title run in the 2026 fall season after finishing last year with a 10-2 record and a district championship. A second-round playoff exit left the team determined to advance further in postseason play. Head coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players who came through the program's middle school ranks. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

With a veteran senior class leading the way, Saint Andrew's has scheduled more challenging opponents this fall to compete at the next level. Senior Jack Williams said the team wants to attract new players by playing against strong teams. Senior Jack Whelche said a better year means going farther in the playoffs, noting that going undefeated in the regular season does not matter if the team keeps losing in the second round. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the daily summer workouts add up as motivation to break team records when the season begins.

cards.headline: St. Lucie Mets Drop Pitching Duel to Tampa Tarpons at Clover Park
cards.teaser: The St. Lucie Mets could not break through offensively Friday night, falling 1-0 to the Tampa Tarpons in a sharp pitching matchup at Clover Park. The game drew 3,797 fans and featu
cards.body:
The St. Lucie Mets could not break through offensively Friday night, falling 1-0 to the Tampa Tarpons in a sharp pitching matchup at Clover Park. The game drew 3,797 fans and featured strong pitching from both clubs, but one second-inning run was enough for Tampa. The loss marked the eighth straight for St. Lucie, while Tampa extended its winning streak to seven games.

Tarpons starter Henry Lalane controlled the game for seven innings, striking out 11 Mets batters while allowing just three hits and no walks. Lalane continued a dominant stretch after striking out 12 batters over seven innings in his previous start against Dunedin, a performance that earned him Florida State League Pitcher of the Week honors.

St. Lucie answered with a strong bullpen-game effort of its own. Starter Christian Rodriguez worked a season-high 3.2 innings and struck out seven. He allowed the game's only run in the second inning after Brando Mayea opened the frame with a double and Engelth Urena followed with a one-out RBI single.

After Rodriguez exited, the Mets' bullpen kept the game within reach. Tyler McLoughlin retired all seven batters he faced across 2.1 perfect innings, striking out five. Kevin Herget, pitching on a MiLB rehab assignment, added two scoreless innings with two strikeouts. Ernesto Mercedes then worked a clean ninth inning, striking out two batters on just eight pitches.

Altogether, four Mets pitchers combined for 16 strikeouts and did not issue a walk.

The Mets had their best chance in the bottom of the ninth, loading the bases with two outs against Jose Ledesma. Tampa brought in Matthew Tippie for the final out, and he ended the threat by getting Branny De Oleo to ground back to the mound.

Trey Snyder led St. Lucie at the plate, going 2-for-4 with a double.

The Mets fell to 2-9 in the second half and 35-42 overall. Tampa improved to 10-3 in the second half and 45-34 overall.

The teams continue their series Saturday at Clover Park with a special 2:50 p.m. start for the 250 Tailgate Party. Fans can get $5 tickets, with $2.50 select beer, hot dogs, fountain soda and popcorn available during the promotion.

hero.headline: Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach offers sea turtle programs through September
hero.body:
Loggerhead Marinelife Center in Juno Beach is offering educational and interactive programs during peak sea turtle nesting season through September. Guests can participate in guided Turtle Walks, the Hatchling Discovery Program, Hatchling Releases, Tidal Tots and Plastic Free July Community Action Day. The center designed these programs to help visitors learn about sea turtle conservation at one of the world's busiest sea turtle nesting beaches.

The Turtle Walk program allows participants to observe the nesting process while learning about sea turtle biology, conservation and research efforts. Educational demonstrations may include red-light headlamps, amber lighting, night scopes and research tag scanning equipment. The center's education and research departments work together during nesting season to collect and analyze data on nesting activity and hatchling success. Sea turtle nesting season in Florida typically runs from March through October. Conservation groups continue encouraging beachgoers to turn off beachfront lighting at night, properly dispose of trash and avoid disturbing nesting turtles or hatchlings. Registration information and program details are available through Loggerhead Marinelife Center.

cards.headline: North Palm Beach hosts Fourth of July fireworks and pool party at country club
cards.teaser: North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse will host a full day of Independence Day activities including a pool party, live music, lawn games and fireworks at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
North Palm Beach residents and visitors will celebrate Independence Day with a full day of family-friendly activities, live entertainment and fireworks at North Palm Beach Country Club and The Clubhouse on July 4. Organizers say this years event also recognizes Americas 250th anniversary, bringing an added sense of celebration to the annual holiday tradition in Palm Beach County.

The free community event begins with a community pool party from 11 a.m. at the country club pool area. Guests can enjoy a water slide, DJ entertainment, games and activities, food and beverages and a poolside satellite bar. Beginning at 4:30 p.m., families can take part in activities including cornhole, Connect 4, giant Jenga, face painting and lawn games. Live music from Solstice Reign is expected to begin around 6 p.m.

Ashley Shipman, director of parks and recreation, said the golf course will offer one of the best locations to watch the fireworks display. The Clubhouse will also host a Fourth of July barbecue buffet from 4:30 p.m. The fireworks finale is scheduled for 9 p.m.

hero.headline: Florida state parks waive admission fees for America's 250th Independence Day
hero.teaser: The Florida Department of Environmental Protection is offering free admission to state parks from July 3 through July 5 to celebrate the nation's semiquincentennial.
hero.body:
The Florida Department of Environmental Protection announced that all residents and visitors can explore state parks free of charge from Friday, July 3, 2026, through Sunday, July 5, 2026, in honor of America's 250th anniversary. DEP Secretary Alexis A. invited all Floridians, their friends and family to the state parks to enjoy the outdoors, make new memories and support treasured public lands. Florida's state parks offer outdoor recreation opportunities including hiking, camping, wildlife viewing, swimming, paddling and horseback riding. The parks also feature historic sites such as forts, battlefields, archaeological sites and other landmarks.

The Florida State Park system is the only four-time winner of the NRPA's National Gold Medal Award. Over the last fiscal year, Florida State Parks saw more than 28 million visitors, generating an estimated 3.6 billion in statewide economic impact. Free admission applies to day use only and excludes Ellie Schiller Homosassa Springs Wildlife State Park, Skyway Fishing Pier State Park and Weeki Wachee Springs State Park. All other fees, including overnight accommodations, special events, concessions and rentals, remain in effect.

cards.headline: DeSantis signs $117.6 billion Florida budget with $810 million in vetoes
cards.body:
Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a $117.6 billion state budget this week, marking the fourth consecutive year of declining spending. The term-limited Governor exercised his veto pen to cut nearly $810 million in line-item appropriations, though he said he was not trying to set a record after vetoing $3.1 billion in 2022. DeSantis described the vetoed items as either inappropriate or nice to have.

The new budget invests billions to accelerate road construction projects, increase teacher pay and make major investments in cancer research. It sets aside $665 million for restoring the Everglades. However, DeSantis vetoed $91.5 million intended to increase correctional officers' salaries. The Legislature had also proposed transferring $750 million into the state's rainy-day fund to prepare for a new constitutional requirement, but that transfer was among the cuts.

Government watchdog Florida TaxWatch had urged DeSantis to eliminate 621 budget projects worth $830 million that the group labeled as turkeys. The Governor vetoed 184 of those 621 appropriations. The House passed a proposed constitutional amendment last year that would increase the mandated cap on the budget stabilization fund, prompting the Legislature to include the potential $750 million transfer this year.

DeSantis indicated he would not formally lead any political committee to campaign for proposed amendments after the Legislature changed his proposals, though he left open the possibility of participating if asked. The budget represents the final major spending plan of DeSantis' tenure as Governor, capping years of aggressive use of veto power to shape state priorities.

cards.headline: Secretary of State Byrd moves to block Paula Stark from House District 47 ballot
cards.teaser: Secretary of State Cord Byrd is asking courts to keep Paula Stark off the ballot after she failed to submit required paperwork before the qualifying deadline.
cards.body:
Secretary of State Cord Byrd filed a response in Leon Circuit Court seeking to keep St. Cloud Republican Paula Stark off the ballot for House District 47 after she failed to properly submit Form 6, a public disclosure of financial interests. Stark's incomplete qualifying materials were timestamped less than 30 minutes before the noon deadline on June 12. Five state employees gave sworn written declarations that Stark's treasurer and partner, Joel Davis, never submitted Form 6 nor was he accidentally handed it back when he submitted the rest of the paperwork. Byrd stated that Stark and Davis knew Form 6 was a required filing and should have exercised care by questioning why it was allegedly handed back or by submitting documents before the deadline.

Election Records Division Bureau Chief Erica Ikay Reeve said Stark was one of 12 candidates who didn't properly turn in Form 6. Half of them corrected the problems and still qualified. Three weeks after the qualifying deadline passed, Stark had not submitted Form 6. Reeve noted that Stark's campaign filed a campaign finance report over one month late, reported excessive contributions, and has an incorrect address on file. The state revoked Stark's Friends of Paula political committee in November over 16,000 dollars in unpaid fines from missed campaign finance deadlines. If Stark is not on the ballot, the August Primary for House District 47 would be open to all voters to decide between Democrats Jorge Figueroa and Anthony Nieves.

cards.headline: Southwest Florida communities celebrate America's 250th with fireworks and parades
cards.teaser: Communities from Sarasota to Fort Myers Beach are marking the semiquincentennial with Fourth of July events including water parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations.
cards.body:
Fourth of July weekend is bringing fireworks, parades, drone shows and waterfront celebrations across Southwest Florida as communities mark America's 250th birthday. The semiquincentennial gives this year's Independence Day events a special anniversary hook, with festivities planned from Sarasota's bayfront and Nathan Benderson Park to Manatee County, Venice, North Port and Fort Myers Beach.

Sarasota's bayfront will host a city co-sponsored America250 fireworks display beginning at 9 p.m. Waterside Place in Lakewood Ranch will celebrate with circus acts, carnival games, a kids zone, food and a drone show over the water at 9 p.m. Siesta Beach will host its 35th annual community fireworks show from 8 to 9:30 p.m., with fireworks launching at dusk. The display is funded entirely by local residents, businesses and community supporters. Fort Myers will celebrate with a free concert by Deb The Dynamics and a fireworks and drone show at the Caloosa Sound Amphitheater. Fort Myers Beach will kick off celebrations with a parade at 10 a.m. starting at Bay Oaks Recreation Center and heading down Estero Boulevard to Times Square, followed by fireworks launched from a barge near Times Square around 9 p.m. Matanzas Pass Bridge will close from around 8:30 to 11:30 p.m. for the fireworks display.

cards.headline: Delray Beach opens 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule for America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Delray Beach will open a time capsule from 1976 during its Fourth of July celebration, an official America250 partner event drawing upward of 20,000 people.
cards.body:
Delray Beach's Fourth of July Celebration, a family-friendly tradition drawing upward of 20,000 people for more than 50 years, is an official America250 partner event marking the nation's 250th anniversary. On the Main Stage at A1A, the city will open a 1976 Bicentennial Time Capsule containing a message from those who celebrated America's 200th birthday to those marking its 250th. At 6 p.m., a 60-foot flag will rise at Atlantic Avenue and Seabreeze Avenue alongside the National Anthem and a reading of the Declaration of Independence by the Delray Beach Historical Society.

Beach activities begin at 8 a.m. with the 4's on the 4th volleyball tournament and the Star Spangled Sandcastles contest, a sand-sculpting competition presented by local Rotary and Kiwanis clubs with judging at 11 a.m. keeping creations patriotic, not political. From noon to 1 p.m., guided snorkel and scuba tours explore the S.S. Inchulva, the British steamship torn apart by an 1903 hurricane 150 yards offshore. Evening entertainment features tribute act Let's Groove Tonight channeling Earth, Wind and Fire and DJ SoNyce on the Main Stage, with Digital Vibez on the East Road Stage from 6:30 to 9 p.m. A Zambelli fireworks display lights the Atlantic at 9 p.m. Road closures run noon to 11 p.m. on East Atlantic and A1A. Free FreeBee rides circulate downtown for visitors parking west of the Intracoastal Bridge. For details, call Parks and Recreation at (561) 243-7250, option 3.

cards.headline: Marion County stages synchronized fireworks at four locations for 250th celebration
cards.teaser: Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four sites under the Marion Celebrates 250 banner, with entertainment beginning at 5 p.m. and fireworks at 9 p.m.
cards.body:
Marion County will stage synchronized fireworks displays at four sites on July 4, each beginning at 5 p.m. with live entertainment, food vendors and family activities before fireworks light up the sky at 9 p.m. The locations are Veterans Memorial Park in Ocala, Wrigley Fields in Citra, Dunnellon High School in Dunnellon and the Belleview Sportsplex in Belleview. The celebrations are part of Marion Celebrates 250, the county's observance of America's semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the signing of the Declaration of Independence.

The city of Ocala hosts Fourth in the Park at Tuscawilla Park starting at 10 a.m., a free celebration with live music, food trucks, a kids zone and games. Ocala-based country singer-songwriter Emma Forgette performs from 10 to 11:30 a.m., followed by Nashville recording artist Cliff Dorsey from noon to 2 p.m. The city is also opening its aquatic fun centers, splash pads and the Discovery Center for free patriotic pool parties and activities. The Patriot Parade kicks off at Southeast 16th Avenue, heads up Silver Springs Boulevard and wraps up near Southeast 25th Avenue, with veteran groups, local businesses and community organizations marching in the early evening.

cards.headline: Voting rights advocate says America's 250th anniversary should renew focus on ballot access
cards.teaser: Constitutional scholar Michael Waldman argues the semiquincentennial celebration should emphasize the ongoing struggle to expand and protect voting rights in America.
cards.body:
Michael Waldman interviewed colleague Jesse Wegman for an upcoming episode of the Briefing podcast about Wegman's new book, The Lost Founder: James Wilson and the Forgotten Fight for a People's Constitution. Wilson was one of only six people to sign both the Declaration of Independence and the Constitution. Waldman argues the celebration of the country's 250th anniversary must be more than fireworks and tall ships, reminding Americans that the nation's story is a long struggle to fulfill the promise of the Declaration of Independence.

From the start, the right to vote required a fight to vote. In 1776, only white men who owned property had the franchise. Pennsylvania's radical new charter gave the right to vote to all men, even those without property, and historians believe to many Black men, with Benjamin Franklin as the principal author. Meanwhile, John Adams warned that expanding suffrage would lead to new claims. Waldman traces the expansion of voting rights through American history: the property requirement ended during Andrew Jackson's presidency, Black men won the right to vote after the Civil War through the 15th Amendment, women won through the 19th Amendment, and the Voting Rights Act of 1965 created a multiracial democracy for the first time. Waldman argues that people in power are again trying to roll back the right to vote, making the semiquincentennial an appropriate moment to focus on ballot access.

hero.headline: Martin County maritime teams deploy two boats with medics for Fourth of July weekend boating safety
hero.teaser: Hundreds of boaters are hitting Martin County waterways this Fourth of July weekend as maritime response teams station two boats with medics in the north and so.
hero.body:
Hundreds of boaters are hitting Martin County waterways this Fourth of July weekend, prompting the Maritime Response Unit to deploy two boats with medics stationed in the north and south parts of the county. Lt. Brett Harry with Martin County Maritime Response Unit said his team will be on standby to assist with everything from minor injuries like stubbed toes to cardiac events and potential spinal injuries.

Boaters launched Friday from Sandsprit Park in Martin County, including Brendan and Ashley Shannon, who brought their young daughter and puppy on the water. The Shannon family said safety is their top priority when hitting the water during the holiday weekend. Lt. Harry urged boaters to keep their eyes on the water, designate a sober driver, and pack life vests, whistles and flotation devices to ensure safety across Martin County waterways throughout the weekend.

cards.headline: Fire agencies extinguish abandoned structure fire in Jensen Beach
cards.teaser: Multiple fire agencies responded to an abandoned structure fire in Jensen Beach on Saturday.
cards.body:
Fire crews extinguished a fire at an abandoned structure in Jensen Beach on Saturday morning. Multiple agencies responded to the scene to bring the blaze under control.

The fire occurred in Jensen Beach, though the exact location of the abandoned structure was not specified. Agencies worked together to suppress the flames and secure the site.

cards.headline: Record 72.2 million Americans traveling for Fourth of July as AAA tracks heavy traffic
cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday.
cards.body:
A record 72.2 million Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with 61.4 million making the trip by car between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, according to AAA estimates. Heavy rain on Friday complicated the journey for South Florida drivers on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd described the conditions, saying "Really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Despite the weather challenges, some drivers navigated the crowded roads without incident. Carlos Borras reported smooth sailing on his round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday, saying "I don't think I saw any traffic, no accidents or anything, so it's been great." However, driver Fernando Amado experienced heavier congestion, noting "It's been pretty busy, especially with the weather" and observing that people were heading north on Friday.

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends departing after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% as ground beef and strawberry prices rise
cards.teaser: A Fourth of July cookout for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation.
cards.body:
The Fourth of July cookout tradition is getting more expensive this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, up 4% from a year ago. The price increases are driven by inflation across multiple items. Ground beef prices have risen 5.5%, buns are up 7.7%, and strawberries have jumped 12.4% due to a Florida frost. Ice cream prices have also increased by 5.3%.

Not all cookout staples have become more costly. Potato prices have decreased this year, offering savings for those planning to buy potato chips and salads. Corn prices have fluctuated, though locally grown corn from the Glades can provide the best deals. Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends families compare prices across stores to find the best deals on their grocery lists. She emphasized that cutting down on food waste is critical for controlling holiday cookout costs, and that process begins with creating a meal plan.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: The School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the state for the third year in a row, with 143 schools rated A or B.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an "A" rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year, reflecting strong student performance across all grade levels. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, received "A" or "B" ratings, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district also achieved a record 93.5% graduation rate. District leaders reported that 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework by taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. Additionally, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach experienced one of the district's biggest success stories, jumping from a "C" rating to an "A" rating this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has served in that role for 15 years following five years as assistant principal, led the turnaround effort. Three years ago, the school modified its early childhood curriculum program, and those students are now in third grade performing at higher levels. Community member Chris Ceasar, who attended Spady as a child and has family members enrolled there, said the jump represents a significant accomplishment for the community. Three other district schools also improved from "C" to "A" ratings: Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: Riviera Beach is one of just 10 U.S. communities to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
The City of Riviera Beach was named one of 10 communities in the United States to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver. The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949 and is considered one of the nation's most respected civic honors.

Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through a long-term effort to revitalize Riviera Beach and improve quality of life for residents. Riviera Beach's application highlighted three programs: the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, stating that every event, project, and challenge is overcome because the community shows up for one another.

cards.headline: Treasure Coast communities prepare to celebrate America's 250th anniversary
cards.teaser: Communities across the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are preparing celebrations for America's 250th anniversary.
cards.body:
Communities in the Palm Beaches and Treasure Coast are gearing up to celebrate America's 250th anniversary this weekend. The milestone marks 250 years since the Declaration of Independence was signed in 1776.

Local celebrations are planned across the region as residents mark the historic occasion. The 250th anniversary represents a significant milestone in American history and communities throughout the Treasure Coast are participating in commemorative events.

hero.headline: Record Fourth of July traffic and rain hit Florida Turnpike through South Florida
hero.teaser: A record 72.2 million Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with 61.4 million driving. Heavy rain and crowded roads created challenges on the Florida Turnpike south of Orlando on Friday.
hero.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with heavy rain compounding congestion on South Florida roads. Friday's wet weather created difficult conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will have traveled at least 50 miles from home between Saturday, June 27 and Sunday, July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA.

Drivers experienced mixed conditions on the roads. Ed Budd said conditions were "really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Carlos Borras reported a smooth round trip between Orlando and Miami on Friday, seeing no traffic or accidents. However, Fernando Amado described heavy traffic, particularly with the weather, noting Saturday was the day people were heading north. AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Fort Pierce woman recognized for supporting little free libraries
cards.teaser: A Fort Pierce woman received recognition for her support of little free libraries in the community.
cards.body: A Fort Pierce resident was honored for her contributions to little free libraries. The recognition highlights community involvement in promoting literacy and book access through the informal library network.

cards.headline: Port St. Lucie advances $95 million Midway Road expansion and Florida Turnpike interchange
cards.teaser: Port St.
cards.body:
Port St. Lucie City Council approved the first reading of an ordinance last month to give 7 acres of land to the Florida Department of Transportation for a partial interchange on Florida's Turnpike. Scott Samples, strategic communications manager for Port St. Lucie, said the interchange addresses a significant gap between current Turnpike entrances and exits in the city. Samples explained the interchange is designed to accommodate growth that has already occurred and growth anticipated over the next 20 to 50 years. The city council will vote on final approval at an upcoming meeting.

FDOT is constructing the $95 million Midway Road Widening Project to address congestion and safety. The first phase widens the road from two lanes to four lanes between Selvitz Road and Jenkins Road, which crews are currently working on. The second phase from Jenkins Road to Glades Cut Off Road remains in the design phase with construction anticipated to begin in Summer 2027. FDOT is also improving the Turnpike bridge and adding a partial interchange, both still in the design phase. The project will include bike and pedestrian paths along with sidewalks.

hero.headline: Fourth of July cookout costs up 4% this year across Florida
hero.teaser: A holiday meal for 10 now costs $73.82, up 4% from last year, according to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey.
hero.body:
Floridians planning Fourth of July cookouts will need to dig deeper into their wallets this year. According to the American Farm Bureau Federation's Summer Cookout Cost Survey, hosting a holiday meal for 10 people now costs $73.82, representing a 4% increase compared to last year. The rise in prices reflects broader inflation affecting grocery stores across the state and the nation.

Several key ingredients are driving up cookout expenses. Ground beef prices have climbed 5.5%, while hamburger buns have seen a particularly steep increase of 7.7%. Strawberries have been especially hard hit, rising 12.4% due to damage from a Florida frost. Ice cream, a summer staple, is up 5.3%. These increases show how inflation is touching nearly every aspect of the traditional Fourth of July meal, from the main course to dessert and side dishes.

Not all grocery prices are climbing, however. Potato prices have declined this year, offering relief for shoppers planning to serve potato salads or chips at their celebrations. Corn prices have been more volatile, but locally grown corn from the Glades provides an affordable option for those seeking the best deals. These price drops offer some opportunities for budget-conscious consumers to offset increases in other categories.

Budgeting expert Andrea Woroch recommends several strategies to keep cookout costs manageable. She suggests shopping strategically by comparing prices across different stores to find the best deals for items on your shopping list. Perhaps most importantly, families should focus on reducing food waste, which starts with creating a meal plan before heading to the grocery store. By being intentional about what they purchase and preparing only what they need, Floridians can enjoy their Fourth of July traditions while keeping expenses under control despite this year's inflation-driven price increases.

cards.teaser: AAA estimates 72.2 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles from home this holiday weekend, marking an all-time high for the Fourth of July.
cards.body:
A record number of Americans are traveling this Fourth of July weekend, with AAA estimating 72.2 million will travel at least 50 miles from home between June 27 and July 5, marking an all-time high for the holiday. Of that number, 61.4 million are making the trip by car. South Florida drivers are experiencing heavy rain adding to the challenge on already-crowded roads, with Friday's wet weather creating difficult conditions on the Florida Turnpike heading south of Orlando. Driver Ed Budd described the conditions as "really beautiful until it starts raining and then everyone forgets how to drive." Driver Fernando Amado noted it has been "pretty busy, especially with the weather," adding that Friday was when people were "really heading up North."

Orlando and Miami rank among the top five travel destinations this Independence Day, according to AAA. The agency finds that where you're coming from, where you're going, and what time you leave can all impact your experience on the road. For those still planning to travel, AAA recommends hitting the road after 3 p.m. on Saturday or before 11 a.m. on Sunday to avoid the worst congestion. The heaviest traffic is expected between 10 a.m. on Saturday and between noon and 6 p.m. on Sunday.

cards.headline: Vero Beach community buries time capsule to be opened in 2076
cards.teaser: Vero Beach residents gathered to bury a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed until 2076.
cards.body:
Vero Beach residents gathered to bury a community-wide time capsule that will remain sealed until 2076. The capsule was buried on Friday, July 3.

The time capsule represents a snapshot of life in Vero Beach in 2026. The ceremony brought together residents from across the community to participate in the historic event.

The capsule will be opened 50 years from now in 2076, allowing future generations to see what life was like in their city half a century earlier. The burial took place in Vero Beach on Friday.

Community members who participated in the event will be 50 years older when the time capsule is opened. The project represents a long-term commitment to preserving the history and character of Vero Beach for future residents.

cards.headline: Palm Beach County schools earn third consecutive A rating from state
cards.teaser: For the third year in a row, the School District of Palm Beach County received an A rating from the Florida Department of Education.
cards.body:
The School District of Palm Beach County earned an A rating from the Florida Department of Education for the third consecutive year. This year, 143 district-operated schools, or 84%, were rated A or B, up from 120 schools the previous year. The district's success is reflected in its record-setting 93.5% graduation rate. District leaders said 86% of seniors participated in college-level coursework, taking at least one Advanced Placement, International Baccalaureate, Cambridge Advanced International Certificate of Education, or Dual Enrollment course. In addition, 144 recent graduates earned an associate degree alongside their high school diploma.

S.D. Spady Elementary School in Delray Beach made a dramatic leap from a C rating last year to an A this year. Principal Rona Tata, who has spent 15 years as principal after serving five years as assistant principal, said three years ago staff began modifying the school's early childhood curriculum program, which starts at age 3 and combines with kindergarten. Many of those students are now in third grade and performing at higher levels, contributing to the renewed A rating. Spady was one of four district schools to improve from a C rating to an A this year, along with Dwight D. Eisenhower K-8, Glade View Elementary, and West Gate Elementary.

cards.headline: Riviera Beach named only Florida city to receive 2026 All-America City Award
cards.teaser: The City of Riviera Beach was named one of just 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League.
cards.body:
Riviera Beach has been named one of only 10 communities in the U.S. to receive the 2026 All-America City Award from the National Civic League, making it the only Florida city selected for the honor this year. The prestigious award recognizes communities that bring residents, local government, businesses and organizations together to solve local challenges and create lasting change. The award was announced during the National Civic League conference in Denver.

Riviera Beach's application highlighted several civic engagement programs, including the Riviera Beach Youth Council, which helps high school students become involved in civic leadership and advocacy; the Citizens Leadership Academy, a civic education initiative with a 98% completion rate; and the Neighborhood Reclaim Home Rehabilitation Program, which provides mini-grants to help longtime homeowners make critical repairs. Mayor Douglas Lawson said the city earned the award through long-term revitalization efforts. "Little old Riviera Beach is one of the biggest, brightest, shining stars," Lawson said. Councilwoman KaShamba Miller-Anderson credited residents for the honor, saying "This award is a tribute to the heart and determination of our residents." The All-America City Award has been presented annually since 1949.

cards.headline: Juno Beach fence dispute at JB-7 beach access could cost town thousands
cards.teaser: Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023.
cards.body:
A missing fence at a Juno Beach public beach access point is creating tension between condo residents and summer beachgoers, with a potential fix that could cost the town thousands of dollars. Residents at the Colony Condos say people using the JB-7 public walkway are cutting through their private property since the town removed the old fence in 2023 for safety reasons. Without it, only bushes separate the public access path from private land. Lori Hill, a Colony resident, said the problem peaks in summer with lots of cars parking randomly and beachgoers pushing back bushes while carrying coolers, fishing rods, and lawn chairs. Hill said residents now call the police when confrontations with trespassers occur after previous attempts to tell them it was private property turned confrontational.

The dispute came before the Juno Beach Town Council at a recent meeting, where a town official noted the town is not obligated to install a fence. Vice Mayor Pro Tem DD Halpern said a lower-cost solution may be worth exploring, suggesting the town could help with a lower-cost fence or a combination of split rail and shrubs. The council agreed to take up the fence question as part of its upcoming budget discussions on July 15. Hill said residents are hopeful the town will restore the fence so they can have their landscaping and private parking back.

cards.headline: Saint Andrew's Scots football targets state title after 10-2 season and district championship
cards.teaser: The Saint Andrew's Scots finished last season with a 10-2 record and a district title, but a second-round playoff exit left the team feeling like more was within reach.
cards.body:
The Saint Andrew's Scots are preparing for the 2026 fall football season with their sights set on a state title after finishing last season with a 10-2 record and a district championship. Despite the strong regular season, a second-round playoff exit left the team believing more was possible. Head football coach Jimmy Robertson said most of the seniors are four-year players who came up through the middle school program. "They know how things are run. They had a lot of success in their career, and hopefully their senior year is the best season that we've had," Robertson said.

The program is leaning into a more demanding schedule this fall to reach the next level. Senior Jack Williams said the team wanted to compete against quality opponents. "We really have a challenging schedule for this year because we wanna compete. That's what we wanna do and we wanna take that next level," Williams said. Senior Jack Whelche identified playoff advancement as the key measure of improvement. "A better year is just gonna be going farther in the playoffs. We just gotta go farther than that, that's all that matters," Whelche said. Senior Edmyer St. Jean said the summer workouts provide daily motivation for the season ahead.
